case_name: P.C. Jairath vs Mrs. Amrit Jairath
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed petition under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act for restitution of conjugal rights against respondent in District Court at Calcutta. Respondent then filed petition under Sections 10 and 25 of Hindu Marriage Act for judicial separation and payment of maintenance against petitioner. Petitioner applied to stay Delhi proceedings on ground that earlier petition was pending in Calcutta court.

legal_principles.principle: The maintainability of appeals on uncertain grounds was not intended by the Legislature.
legal_principles.held: It is difficult to conceive that the Legislature left the matter of maintainability of appeals on wholly uncertain grounds and that for finding whether a particular order under this Act was or was not appealable the Legislature intended to leave the parties to have recourse to the provisions of other laws.
cited_cases: Sobhana Sen v. Amar Kanta, (1959) AIR Cal 455
Rukhmanibai v. Kishanlal Ramlal, (1959) AIR Madh Pra 187
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — one reason why the court emphasized the importance of clear legislative intent

legal_principles.principle: The right to appeal against orders under the Hindu Marriage Act is determined by reference to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.
legal_principles.held: Whatever might be the position with respect to decrees and orders made under the specified provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act, so far as the orders on applications under the Code of Civil Procedure are concerned, according to Mr. Kirpal, the right of appeal would only be there if it is provided by that Code.
cited_cases: Sunder Singh v. Manna Sunder Singh, (1962) AIR Punjab 127
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — one reason why the court emphasized the importance of considering the Code of Civil Procedure

outcome.final_order: Order refusing to stay the proceedings was upheld.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for restoration of conjugal rights
responding to a petition for judicial separation
seeking stay of proceedings in a divorce case
